radiantArchitectures.name: Cast Iron Radiants & Heavy Chevron Grates
radiantArchitectures.description: Dense cast iron radiants inverted above gas burners with angled chevron grates designed to channel lipid runoff away from direct flame impingement.

radiantArchitectures.name: 304 Stainless Steel Tent Radiants & Rod Grates
radiantArchitectures.description: Inverted V-shaped 16-gauge stainless steel deflectors over tubular burners; smooth surface allows rapid fat drainage but creates intense localized hot spots.

radiantArchitectures.name: Porous Ceramic Briquette Radiant Bed
radiantArchitectures.description: High-porosity ceramic refractory briquettes held in steel grates; acts as a sponge for dripping oil, leading to continuous sustained smoldering and intense flare-ups.

radiantArchitectures.name: Aged & Carbonized Pitted Cast Iron Radiants
radiantArchitectures.description: Heavily carbonized cast iron with baked-on creosote and grease slag, prone to chronic grease fire initiation and catastrophic volatile resuspension.

radiantArchitectures.name: Hardox Engineered V-Baffle Stainless Charbroiler
radiantArchitectures.description: Advanced commercial charbroiler with laser-cut steep angled grease gutters that direct 85% of liquified animal fat into an external cold water trough.

meatProfiles.name: Ground Chuck Beef Burger (80/20 Blend)
meatProfiles.description: High-fat ground beef patty with rapid lipid rendering; dripping triglycerides ignite instantly upon contacting red-hot radiants.

meatProfiles.name: Center-Cut Sirloin Steak (Trimmed 90/10)
meatProfiles.description: Lean beef primal cut; low fat drip reduces open flame flare-ups, but high surface creatine fosters intense heterocyclic amine (HCA) formation on char marks.

meatProfiles.name: Marinated Pork Belly / Char Siu Ribs
meatProfiles.description: Extreme risk matrix combining high lipid drip rates with sugary marinades that caramelize, foam, and flash-ignite into continuous smoke plumes.

meatProfiles.name: Skin-On Bone-In Chicken Thighs
meatProfiles.description: Polyunsaturated subcutaneous poultry fat drips violently and undergoes radical lipid peroxidation at lower ignition temperatures (310°C).

meatProfiles.name: Commercial Plant-Based Burger (Canola/Coconut Oil)
meatProfiles.description: Contains vegetable oils without muscle creatine; low HCA formation but produces significant aerosolized acrolein and lighter PAH volatile species during flare-ups.

radiantTemperatures.thermalBreakdown: Incomplete fat vaporization; greasy aerosol condensation dominant
Rapid radical fragmentation of triglycerides; active flash flare-ups
Severe gas-phase aromatization; explosive Benzo[a]pyrene generation
Runaway grease combustion; toxic volatile aromatic plume exceeds hood capacity

ventilationProfiles.name: Dedicated NFPA 96 / UL 710 Type I Hood (400 CFM/linear ft)
ventilationProfiles.description: High-velocity proximity canopy hood with baffle filters, makeup air compensation, and 0.45 m/s capture velocity at charbroiler boundary edge.

ventilationProfiles.name: Shared Kitchen Hood with Dirty Baffles (250 CFM/linear ft)
ventilationProfiles.description: Standard exhaust hood shared with fryers and ranges; grease-laden baffles reduce airflow and cause convective plume spillage during heavy flare-ups.

ventilationProfiles.name: Undersized Hood or Cross-Draft Spillage (150 CFM/linear ft)
ventilationProfiles.description: Severe face velocity drop caused by strong makeup air drafts, improper hood overhang, or fan motor belt slippage; toxic plumes flood line cook breathing zone.

pahSpeciesBenchmarks.description: Primary high-potency carcinogen formed during gas-phase free radical recombination above 550°C; deposits onto meat surfaces with rising black smoke.
Four-ring aromatic hydrocarbon released during incomplete lipid pyrolysis; highly persistent in exhaust duct grease.

pahSpeciesBenchmarks.meatLimitEu: Included in PAH4 sum (30.0 µg/kg limit)
pahSpeciesBenchmarks.description: Co-emitted with benzo[a]pyrene during intense open flare-ups on ceramic and cast iron radiants.
Low-molecular-weight volatile PAHs that dominate the gas phase of the charbroiler plume, creating acrid odor and eye irritation.

occupationalThresholds.acgihTlvBap: Exposure by all routes should be carefully controlled to levels as low as possible
occupationalThresholds.nfpa96MinimumExhaust: 300 to 400 CFM per linear foot of heavy-duty cooking equipment
